summary: Ouachita fire tower on Winding Stair Mountain; reported built in 1935, a 1936 notice plans a steel replacement, and the record says removed. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: Fire tower on the highest peak; a 1936 notice describes a 28-foot wood tower and a planned 33-foot steel replacement
facts.status_note: The Forest Lookouts record is marked Removed. No source gives a date or method for the removal.

access.note: The Winding Stair Mountains lie within Winding Stair Mountain National Recreation Area, Ouachita National Forest, which has trails. No source describes access to the former tower site.

events.note: Reported as already constructed in a November 1935 item; a June 1934 item had announced it for that fall
October 1936 notice: 28-foot wood tower in use, 33-foot steel tower announced to replace it; completion not reported
Tom Doyle and Sebe Johnson named as tower guards
Three men alternately worked at the tower
Butane gas system and vented heater being installed; until then the tower had been heated with a small kerosene stove

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A November 1935 item says a 40-foot tower had been constructed on the highest point. An October 1936 notice describes a 28-foot wood tower in use and a 33-foot steel tower to replace it. The record keeps 12.2 m from the 1935 item, but the sources do not show which structure stood on the summit after 1936.

sources.title: Winding Stair Mountain National Recreation Area

notes_for_editor: Source 1 and source 2 reproduce 1934 to 1957 newspaper items (The Paris News, The Daily Oklahoman, Heavener Ledger); the originals were not checked. The Sycamore record may describe the same tower under another name, so check for a duplicate or merge. The brief's access 'unknown' is set to public from the recreation area status; that is an inference, not a stated access rule. Removal date and method are unknown. A WebFetch read of thedirtymule.com (fetch_text got 403) describes an old fire tower site with only the clearing remaining, but that text is not in the fetch cache and is not quoted. A myfamilytravels article covers the Honobia tower, a different structure, and was not used.
